units.title: My school day

words.def: to leave your bed after you wake up
words.ex: On Sundays I stay in bed and ___ at ten o'clock.

words.def: to put your clothes on
words.ex: After my shower I ___: shirt, trousers and shoes.

words.def: to clean something with water and soap
words.ex: Please ___ your hands with soap before lunch.

words.def: work your teacher gives you to do after school
words.ex: I do my maths ___ after school.

words.def: a short time between lessons when you can rest or play
words.ex: We play football in the playground at ___.

words.def: something that is wrong, like a wrong answer
words.ex: Two and two is five? That's a ___!

words.def: quick at learning and understanding things
words.ex: Ana knows all the answers. She's very ___.

words.def: making very little noise
words.ex: Please be ___ in the library. People are reading.

words.def: not hard to do
words.ex: The test was ___. I got all the answers right!

words.def: hard to do or to understand
words.ex: This sum is very ___. Can you help me, please?

words.def: every time
words.ex: I ___ brush my teeth before bed. I never forget!

words.def: sleeping; not awake
words.ex: At ten o'clock at night I'm fast ___ in bed.

words.def: to stop sleeping
words.ex: I ___ when my alarm rings, but I stay in bed for five more minutes.

words.def: to clean your teeth or make your hair tidy
words.ex: I ___ my teeth after breakfast and before bed.

words.def: you stand under it and water comes down to wash your body
words.ex: I stand under the ___ and wash my hair.

words.def: feeling that you need to rest or sleep
words.ex: I went to bed very late, so I'm very ___ this morning.

words.def: a bag you carry your books and pencils to school in

words.def: two pieces of bread with cheese, meat or salad between them
words.ex: For lunch I've got a cheese ___ and an apple.

words.def: a metal thing that rings to tell you a lesson is starting or ending

words.def: not fun or exciting at all
words.ex: Nothing happens in this film. It's so ___!

grammar.q: My sister ___ to school by bus.
grammar.why: With he, she and it, add -s or -es to the verb: she goes.

grammar.q: We ___ lunch at twelve o'clock.
grammar.why: With I, you, we and they, use the verb with no -s: we have.

grammar.q: ___ your brother walk to school?
grammar.why: Ask questions about he, she or it with 'Does': Does he walk?

grammar.q: I ___ like tests.
grammar.why: Use 'don't' with I, you, we and they: I don't like.

grammar.q: She ___ her homework after dinner.
grammar.why: 'Always' goes before the verb, and with she the verb is 'does': she always does.

grammar.q: I get up early, so I am ___ late for school.
grammar.why: 'Never' means not at any time. I get up early, so I'm never late.

grammar.q: My brother ___ a shower every morning.
grammar.why: 'Every morning' means it happens again and again, so use the present simple. My brother = he, so 'has'.

grammar.q: We ___ go to school on Saturdays.
grammar.why: Use 'don't' + verb with I, you, we and they: we don't go.

grammar.q: What time ___ the bell ring?
grammar.why: The bell = it. Ask about it with 'does': What time does it ring?

grammar.q: Our teacher ___ late.
grammar.why: Put 'never', 'always' and 'often' after am, is or are: she is never late.

sentences: My little sister can't get dressed on her own.
What time do you get up?
Our teacher gives us lots of homework.
Does your brother walk to school?
Don't forget your school bag!
What time does the bell ring?

reading.title: Leo's school day
reading.text: Leo gets up at seven o'clock every day. He washes his face, gets dressed and has breakfast with his mum. Then he walks to school with his friend Ben. Lessons start at nine. Leo's favourite lesson is science because it is never boring. At break he plays football in the playground. After school he does his homework. It isn't difficult, but it takes a long time. At nine o'clock Leo is asleep in bed.

qs.q: What time does Leo get up?
Who does Leo walk to school with?
Leo's favourite lesson is maths.
Leo plays football at break.
What does Leo do after school?

reading.title: Mia's late morning
reading.text: On Monday Mia woke up late because her alarm didn't ring. She had a very quick shower and got dressed. There was no time for breakfast, so Dad gave her a cheese sandwich for the bus. Mia got to school just before the bell rang at nine. In the first lesson she opened her school bag. Oh no! Her maths book was at home. 'Don't worry,' said her teacher. 'You can share with Tom.'

qs.q: Why did Mia wake up late?
Mia had breakfast at home.
What did Dad give Mia for the bus?
The bell rang at nine.
What was at home?

extra.q: I ___ my homework after dinner.
extra.why: We say 'do your homework', not 'make' it.

extra.q: School starts ___ nine o'clock.
extra.why: Use 'at' with clock times: at nine o'clock.

extra.q: I have swimming lessons ___ Tuesdays.
extra.why: Use 'on' with days: on Monday, on Tuesdays.

extra.q: It's warm in the classroom. Please ___ your coat.
extra.why: 'Take off' means remove your clothes, like a coat. 'Put on' is the opposite.

units.title: Sports and hobbies

words.def: a team sport where you hit a ball with a long stick
words.ex: In ___, you use a stick to hit the ball into the goal.

words.def: a sport where you move across ice in special boots
words.ex: When the lake turns to ice in winter, we go ___.

words.def: to go up something using your hands and feet
words.ex: Monkeys can ___ trees very quickly.

words.def: to move your body to music
words.ex: When I hear music, I want to ___!

words.def: trying to catch fish with a long stick and a line
words.ex: Grandpa and I go ___ at the river and catch big fish.

words.def: a big place full of water where you can swim
words.ex: We jump into the blue water at the ___ near our school.

words.def: the net you kick or hit the ball into to win a point
words.ex: She kicked the ball into the ___ and her team won!

words.def: a story with moving pictures that you watch on a screen
words.ex: We are going to watch a funny ___ at the cinema.

words.def: to hit something with your foot
words.ex: In football, you ___ the ball with your foot.

words.def: to take and hold something that is moving through the air
words.ex: Throw the ball to me. I can ___ it!

words.def: to jump on one foot
words.ex: Can you ___ on one foot to the end of the playground?

words.def: a magazine with stories told in pictures
words.ex: I'm reading a funny ___ with lots of pictures.

words.def: a game where two teams try to throw a ball through a high round net
words.ex: Tall players are good at ___ because the net is very high.

words.def: a game where two or four players hit a small ball over a net
words.ex: I play ___ with my dad. We hit the ball over the net to each other.

words.def: to travel on water in a boat that the wind pushes
words.ex: On windy days, my uncle likes to ___ his little boat on the lake.

words.def: a round music thing that you hit with sticks or your hands
words.ex: My brother plays the ___ very loudly. Boom, boom, boom!

words.def: a music thing with six strings that you play with your fingers
words.ex: I'm learning to play the ___. It has got six strings.

words.def: to make a picture with colours and a brush
words.ex: Let's ___ a picture of the sea with blue and green colours.

words.def: to be the best or come first in a game or race
words.ex: Run fast! You can ___ the race!

words.def: a group of people who play a sport together
words.ex: There are eleven players in a football ___.

grammar.q: Look! The children ___ football in the park.
grammar.why: Use am, is or are + -ing for what is happening now. The children = they, so 'are playing'.

grammar.q: My dad ___ a book right now. He's on the sofa.
grammar.why: 'Right now' means at this moment, so use is + -ing: he is reading.

grammar.q: I love ___ with my friends.
grammar.why: After 'love' or 'like', use the -ing form: I love dancing.

grammar.q: What ___ you doing? I'm climbing a tree.
grammar.why: Ask about now with 'What are you doing?'

grammar.q: A football is ___ than a tennis ball.
grammar.why: To compare two things, use -er + than: bigger than.

grammar.q: Our team ___ the match last Saturday.
grammar.why: 'Last Saturday' is in the past. 'Win' is irregular: win, won.

grammar.q: She ___ tennis every Saturday.
grammar.why: 'Every Saturday' tells us it happens again and again, so use the present simple: she plays.

grammar.q: We ___ playing basketball. We're watching a film.
grammar.why: Use 'aren't' (are not) + -ing with we, you and they.

grammar.q: Yesterday Ben ___ the ball very high.
grammar.why: 'Throw' is irregular. In the past it is 'threw'.

grammar.q: I think tennis is ___ than hockey.
grammar.why: When a short word ends in -y, change y to i and add -er: easy, easier.

sentences: My brother is climbing a tree.
Do you like ice skating?
She kicked the ball into the goal.
My grandpa loves going fishing.
My sister plays the drums very loudly.
Which team won the match?

reading.title: A busy Saturday
reading.text: It's Saturday and my family is very busy. My sister Emma is playing hockey with her school team. She is faster than the other players! Dad loves fishing, so he is at the river with Grandpa. I like dancing, and I have a dance class at ten o'clock. And Mum? She is sitting on the sofa and reading a comic. That's her favourite hobby!

qs.q: What is Emma playing?
Where is Dad?
Emma is slower than the other players.
What time is the dance class?
Mum is reading a comic.

reading.title: Sam's new hobby
reading.text: Last year Sam didn't have a hobby. He watched cartoons every afternoon. Then his uncle gave him an old drum. Now Sam plays it every day after school! It's very loud, so Mum isn't always happy. Sam's sister plays the guitar, and his friend Ben sings. They have got a band called The Noisy Cats. On Saturday they are going to play at the school party.

qs.q: Who gave Sam a drum?
What does Sam's sister play?
Sam plays the drum every day after school.
Ben plays the guitar in the band.
When are they going to play at the school party?

extra.q: My sister ___ hockey every Saturday.
extra.why: Use 'play' with sports and games: play hockey, play football.

extra.q: On Sundays, Grandpa and I ___ fishing.
extra.why: Use 'go' with many -ing activities: go fishing, go swimming, go skating.

extra.q: I ___ the guitar in a band.
extra.why: Use 'play' with music: play the guitar, play the drums.

extra.q: My brother is very good ___ tennis.
extra.why: We say 'good at' something: good at tennis, good at maths.

units.title: In the town

words.def: a very big town with lots of people and buildings
words.ex: London is a very big ___ with millions of people.

words.def: a very small town in the countryside
words.ex: My grandma lives in a small ___ with only one shop.

words.def: the place by the road where you wait to get on a bus
words.ex: Wait at the ___ and the number 12 bus will come.

words.def: a small place where you can buy drinks and simple food
words.ex: Let's have a hot chocolate and a cake at the ___.

words.def: a building where you watch films on a big screen
words.ex: We are going to the ___ to see a new film.

words.def: a building with lots of books that you can take home and bring back
words.ex: I get books from the ___ and take them back after two weeks.

words.def: a very big shop that sells food and lots of other things
words.ex: We push a trolley around the big ___ and buy milk, bread and soap.

words.def: a place outside with tables where people sell fruit, vegetables and other things
words.ex: On Saturdays, farmers sell fruit and vegetables at the ___ in the square.

words.def: a house, school, shop or office: something with walls and a roof
words.ex: My dad works in a tall ___ with twenty floors.

words.def: a picture that shows where places and roads are
words.ex: We are lost! Let's look at the ___.

words.def: a long hard way for cars, buses and bikes
words.ex: Look left and right before you cross the ___.

words.def: to visit shops and buy things
words.ex: On Saturdays, Mum and I ___ for new clothes.

words.def: a building where trains stop so that people can get on and off
words.ex: The train leaves from the ___ at ten o'clock.

words.def: a place where people can leave their cars
words.ex: Dad left the car in the ___ next to the supermarket.

words.def: a car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere
words.ex: It's late and there are no buses, so let's take a ___ home.

words.def: a place that keeps people's money safe
words.ex: Mum is getting some money from the ___.

words.def: a road or path that goes over a river so you can cross it
words.ex: We walked over the old ___ and looked down at the river.

words.def: a place where you can send letters and buy stamps
words.ex: I'm going to the ___ to send a letter to my cousin.

words.def: an open place in the middle of a town, with buildings all around it
words.ex: There is a big market in the town ___ on Saturdays.

words.def: forward, without turning left or right
words.ex: Don't turn left or right. Go ___ and the cinema is at the end of the road.

grammar.q: There aren't ___ shops in my village.
grammar.why: Use 'any' after 'not': there aren't any shops.

grammar.q: There are ___ new books in the library.
grammar.why: Use 'some' in positive sentences about more than one thing.

grammar.q: A village is ___ than a city.
grammar.why: Short words add -er to compare: small, smaller than.

grammar.q: The new cafe is ___ than the old one.
grammar.why: 'Good' is special: good, better.

grammar.q: Last Saturday we ___ to the cinema.
grammar.why: 'Go' is irregular. In the past it is 'went'.

grammar.q: Yesterday we ___ around the market.
grammar.why: For the past, add -ed to most verbs: walk, walked.

grammar.q: We need ___ bread from the supermarket.
grammar.why: Use 'some' in positive sentences, also with words like bread and milk.

grammar.q: The new library is ___ than the old one.
grammar.why: Long words use 'more' to compare: more beautiful than.

grammar.q: Last night we ___ a taxi to the station.
grammar.why: 'Take' is irregular. In the past it is 'took'.

grammar.q: We ___ go to the bank yesterday. It was closed.
grammar.why: For 'not' in the past, use 'didn't' + verb: we didn't go.

sentences: Is there a library in your town?
My village hasn't got any shops.
Which bus goes to the city centre?
Where can I buy a map?
Let's take a taxi to the station.
Is there a car park near here?

reading.title: A day in the city
reading.text: Last Saturday Kate went to the city with her grandma. They took the bus from the bus stop near Kate's house. First they went to a big market in the square. Grandma bought some apples and flowers. Then they walked to the library, and Kate chose two books about animals. They were hungry, so they had lunch at a little cafe. Kate had a sandwich and a hot chocolate. It was a great day!

qs.q: Who did Kate go to the city with?
How did they go to the city?
Kate chose two books about cars.
Where did they have lunch?
Kate had a hot chocolate.

reading.title: Where is the station?
reading.text: Paul and his dad are in a new city. They want to go to the train station, but they can't find it. Dad asks a woman at the bus stop. 'Go straight on, past the bank,' she says. 'Then walk over the bridge. The station is next to a big car park.' They walk for ten minutes and cross the old bridge. There it is! Their train leaves in five minutes, so they run.

qs.q: Where do Paul and his dad want to go?
Who does Dad ask for help?
opts: a woman at the bus stop

qs.q: The station is next to a big car park.
They take a taxi to the station.
Why do they run?
opts: Their train leaves in five minutes.

extra.q: The cafe is ___ the library and the bank.
extra.why: Use 'between' for something in the middle of two places.

extra.q: Turn left, and the cinema is ___ your right.
extra.why: We say 'on your right' and 'on your left'.

extra.q: We walked ___ the bridge to the other side of the river.
extra.why: 'Across' means from one side to the other side.

extra.q: This is our stop. Let's ___ the bus here.
extra.why: 'Get off' means leave a bus or a train. 'Get on' means go into it.

units.title: Weather and seasons

words.def: how it is outside: sunny, rainy, windy, hot or cold
words.ex: What's the ___ like today? It's sunny and warm.

words.def: bright, with lots of light from the sun
words.ex: Put on your sunglasses. It's very ___ today!

words.def: when the sky is grey and you can't see the sun
words.ex: It's ___ today, so I can't see the sun or the blue sky.

words.def: water that falls from the sky in drops
words.ex: I need my umbrella because of the ___.

words.def: soft white ice that falls from the sky when it's very cold
words.ex: The garden is all white because of the ___.

words.def: with a lot of air moving fast outside
words.ex: It's ___ today. Let's fly a kite!

words.def: seven colours in a big curve across the sky
words.ex: After the rain, we saw a beautiful ___ in the sky.

words.def: covered in water; not dry
words.ex: I didn't take my umbrella, so my hair is ___.

words.def: the time of year after winter, when flowers start to grow
words.ex: In ___, the trees get new green leaves.

words.def: the hot time of the year, between spring and autumn
words.ex: We go to the beach in ___ because it's hot.

words.def: the time of year after summer, when leaves fall from the trees
words.ex: In ___, the leaves turn red and brown and fall from the trees.

words.def: the cold time of the year, after autumn
words.ex: In ___, it's very cold and sometimes it snows.

words.def: you hold it over your head to stay dry when it rains
words.ex: It's raining! Take your ___ so you don't get wet.

words.def: water that is so cold that it becomes hard
words.ex: Put some ___ in my juice, please. It's very hot today.

words.def: a warm jacket, often long, that you wear outside when it's cold
words.ex: My winter ___ is long and warm, and it has got big pockets.

words.def: a long piece of cloth that you wear around your neck to keep warm
words.ex: It's cold, so I'm wearing a ___ around my neck.

words.def: dark glasses that you wear when the sun is bright
words.ex: The sun is very bright. Put on your ___!

words.def: spring, summer, autumn or winter: one of the four parts of the year
words.ex: My favourite ___ is spring because I love the flowers.

words.def: with no water on it; not wet
words.ex: My hair is wet. Can I have a towel to get ___?

words.def: the space above you, where you can see the sun, the moon and clouds
words.ex: Look up at the ___! It's blue and there are no clouds.

grammar.q: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain.
grammar.why: Use 'is going to' when you can see that something will happen. With it, use 'is'.

grammar.q: We ___ visit Grandma in the summer.
grammar.why: Use 'are going to' with we, you and they for plans.

grammar.q: Today is ___ than yesterday. I need a coat!
grammar.why: To compare, add -er + than: cold, colder than.

grammar.q: Summer is ___ than winter.
grammar.why: Hot, hotter: double the t, then add -er.

grammar.q: Take an umbrella. It ___ outside.
grammar.why: Use is + -ing for things that are happening now.

grammar.q: It's very hot here in summer, so it ___ snows.
grammar.why: 'Never' means not at any time. It's hot, so it never snows.

grammar.q: I ___ going to wear my new scarf tomorrow.
grammar.why: With 'going to', use 'am' with I: I am going to wear it.

grammar.q: It ___ often snow here. It's warm in winter.
grammar.why: The weather = it. Use 'doesn't' + verb with it: it doesn't snow.

grammar.q: Was it sunny yesterday? No, it ___ cloudy.
grammar.why: 'Yesterday' is in the past. Use 'was' with it: it was cloudy.

grammar.q: In my country it ___ rains in autumn.
grammar.why: Put 'often' before most verbs: it often rains.

sentences: What is the weather like?
My coat is wet from the rain.
We are going to build a snowman.
Look at that beautiful rainbow!
I'm going to wear my new scarf.
Which season do you like best?

reading.title: Four seasons
reading.text: There are four seasons in my country. In spring it often rains, and the flowers start to grow. Summer is hot and sunny, so we go swimming in the sea. In autumn it is windy, and the leaves fall from the trees. Winter is very cold. Sometimes it snows, and we make a snowman in the garden. My favourite season is summer because I love the beach!

qs.q: When do the flowers start to grow?
What do they do in summer?
opts: They go swimming in the sea.

qs.q: It is windy in autumn.
The writer's favourite season is winter.
Where do they make a snowman?

reading.title: A snow day
reading.text: Yesterday it snowed all day, so there was no school! Ella put on her warm coat, her scarf and her boots. She went into the garden with her brother. The sky was grey and the snow was soft. They made a big snowman and gave him Dad's old hat. Then they played in the snow with their friends. When they came inside, their hands were wet and cold. Mum made them hot chocolate.

qs.q: Why was there no school?
What did they give the snowman?
The sky was blue.
Their hands were wet and cold when they came inside.
What did Mum make?

extra.q: My birthday is ___ summer.
extra.why: Use 'in' with seasons and months: in summer, in July.

extra.q: What does 'It's boiling today!' mean?
extra.why: When people say 'It's boiling!' about the weather, they mean it's very, very hot.

extra.q: There's a strong ___ today. Hold on to your hat!
extra.why: We say 'strong wind', but 'heavy rain' and 'heavy snow'.

extra.q: I took my umbrella ___ it was raining.
extra.why: Use 'because' to give a reason: I took it because it was raining.

units.title: My body and health

words.def: the part of your body between your head and your shoulders
words.ex: A giraffe has got a very long ___.

words.def: the part of your body between your neck and your arm
words.ex: The parrot is sitting on the pirate's ___.

words.def: the part of your body behind you, from your neck down to your legs
words.ex: Lie on your ___ and look up at the stars.

words.def: the part inside your body where food goes after you eat it
words.ex: I ate too much cake and now my ___ hurts.

words.def: the hard white things in your mouth that you bite with
words.ex: Brush your ___ twice a day.

words.def: a pain in your head
words.ex: The music is very loud and now I've got a ___.

words.def: a small illness that makes you sneeze and cough
words.ex: I've got a ___, so I need lots of tissues for my nose.

words.def: when your body is too hot because you are ill
words.ex: You're very hot. I think you've got a ___.

words.def: a person whose job is to help ill people get better
words.ex: I feel ill, so Mum is taking me to see the ___.

words.def: a big building where doctors and nurses look after very ill people
words.ex: My baby brother was born in this ___.

words.def: something you take when you are ill, to help you get better
words.ex: Take this ___ three times a day and you will feel better.

words.def: to have a pain somewhere in your body
words.ex: My legs ___ after the long walk.

words.def: one of the two parts of your head that you hear with
words.ex: My ___ hurts, so I can't hear very well.

words.def: the part of your face that you smell with
words.ex: Mmm! My ___ can smell Mum's cake from the garden.

words.def: the part at the end of your leg that you stand on
words.ex: This shoe is too small for my ___.

words.def: hair that grows on the lower part of a man's face
words.ex: Grandpa has got a long white ___ like Father Christmas.

words.def: with a body that can lift and carry heavy things
words.ex: My big brother is very ___. He can carry me on his back!

words.def: feeling ill, often in your stomach
words.ex: I ate too many sweets and now I feel ___.

words.def: to push air out of your mouth with a short loud noise when you are ill
words.ex: Please put your hand over your mouth when you ___.

words.def: a person in a hospital who looks after ill people and helps the doctors
words.ex: The ___ gave me some water and helped the doctor.

grammar.q: You ___ brush your teeth every day.
grammar.why: 'Must' means it is very important to do it.

grammar.q: You ___ eat lots of sweets. They're bad for your teeth.
grammar.why: 'Mustn't' means don't do it.

grammar.q: What's the matter? My stomach ___.
grammar.why: My stomach = it, so add -s: it hurts.

grammar.q: Yesterday I ___ over in the playground.
grammar.why: 'Fall' is irregular. In the past it is 'fell'.

grammar.q: Last week Tom ___ a bad cold.
grammar.why: 'Have' is irregular. In the past it is 'had'.

grammar.q: ___ you go to the doctor yesterday?
grammar.why: Ask questions about the past with 'Did'.

grammar.q: My ears ___ because the music is very loud.
grammar.why: 'My ears' means more than one (they), so the verb has no -s: they hurt.

grammar.q: Last night I ___ a lot because of my cold.
grammar.why: 'Last night' is in the past. Add -ed to the verb: cough, coughed.

grammar.q: ___ you feel better now? Yes, thank you.
grammar.why: Ask 'Do you...?' with you and a verb like 'feel'.

grammar.q: He ___ stay in bed today.
grammar.why: 'Must' never changes and has no 'to' after it: he must stay.

sentences: You must drink lots of water.
Has your sister got a temperature?
The doctor gave me some medicine.
What's the matter with your back?
The nurse looked at my sore foot.
My grandpa has got a white beard.

reading.title: Max stays at home
reading.text: Last Monday Max didn't go to school. He woke up with a headache and a cough, and he had a temperature. His mum took him to the doctor. The doctor said, 'You've got a bad cold. You must stay in bed for two days and drink lots of water.' Max took his medicine and slept a lot. On Wednesday he felt better, and he went back to school.

qs.q: When did Max wake up with a headache?
Who took Max to the doctor?
The doctor said Max had a bad cold.
Max had to stay in bed for a week.
When did Max go back to school?

reading.title: Lucy and the school nurse
reading.text: Last Tuesday, Lucy hurt her foot in a hockey game at school. It wasn't bad, but she couldn't walk very well. Her teacher took her to the school nurse. The nurse looked at her foot and put some ice on it. 'You must rest it for two days,' she said. 'And you mustn't play hockey this week.' Lucy was sad, but the next Monday her foot was better and she played again.

qs.q: How did Lucy hurt her foot?
Who took Lucy to the nurse?
The nurse put some ice on Lucy's foot.
The nurse said Lucy must rest for a week.
What mustn't Lucy do this week?

extra.q: I've got a pain ___ my stomach.
extra.why: Use 'in' for a pain inside your body: a pain in my stomach.

extra.q: I ___ a bad cough.
extra.why: We say 'have got' a cough, a cold or a headache.

extra.q: I hope you ___ better soon!
extra.why: We say 'get better' when an ill person starts to feel well again.

extra.q: Brush your teeth ___ (careful).
extra.why: Use an adverb with -ly to say how you do something: brush carefully.

units.title: In the kitchen

words.def: to make food hot so you can eat it, for example in an oven
words.ex: Dad likes to ___ fish and rice for dinner.

words.def: a flat round dish that you put food on
words.ex: Put your chips on your ___ and come to the table.

words.def: a round deep dish for soup, rice or cereal
words.ex: I eat my cereal from a big ___ with a spoon.

words.def: a small round thing with a handle that you drink hot drinks from
words.ex: Would you like a ___ of tea, Grandma?

words.def: you drink water or juice from it, and you can see through it
words.ex: Put the orange juice in a tall ___ with some ice.

words.def: a small thing with a round end that you use to eat soup
words.ex: You eat soup with a ___, not with a fork.

words.def: a thing with three or four points that you use to pick up food
words.ex: Hold your ___ in your left hand and your knife in your right.

words.def: a tall thing, often made of glass or plastic, for drinks like water or milk
words.ex: There is a ___ of water in my school bag.

words.def: a cold cupboard in the kitchen that keeps food fresh
words.ex: The cheese and the milk are in the ___ to keep them cold.

words.def: a thin, flat, round cake that you cook in a pan
words.ex: I like my ___ with lemon and sugar.

words.def: a hot food made from vegetables or meat in water, that you eat with a spoon
words.ex: It's cold outside, so let's have some hot tomato ___.

words.def: a cold mix of vegetables like tomatoes and green leaves
words.ex: I'm making a ___ with tomatoes, carrots and green leaves.

words.def: a yellow or white food made from milk
words.ex: Pizza has got tomato and ___ on it.

words.def: food from animals, like chicken or beef
words.ex: Lions eat ___. They don't eat grass.

words.def: a sweet, sticky, yellow food that bees make
words.ex: Bears love sweet ___.

words.def: small white bits that you put on food to make it taste better
words.ex: Sea water tastes of ___.

words.def: a plant that we eat, like a carrot or a potato
words.ex: My favourite ___ is broccoli.

words.def: wanting to eat
words.ex: I didn't have breakfast, so I'm very ___ now.

words.def: with a very good taste
words.ex: Mmm! This chocolate cake is ___!

words.def: very warm; the opposite of cold
words.ex: Don't touch the pan. It's very ___!

grammar.q: Are there ___ eggs in the fridge?
grammar.why: Use 'any' in questions: Are there any eggs?

grammar.q: We haven't got ___ milk. Let's buy some.
grammar.why: Use 'any' after 'not': we haven't got any milk.

grammar.q: Children ___ use the oven without a grown-up.
grammar.why: 'Mustn't' means it is not allowed. Don't use the oven on your own!

grammar.q: Dad ___ pancakes right now. Can you smell them?
grammar.why: 'Right now' means at this moment, so use is + -ing: he is making.

grammar.q: I'm ___ make a cake for Grandma's birthday tomorrow.
grammar.why: Use am, is or are + 'going to' + verb for plans.

grammar.q: Yesterday we ___ soup for lunch.
grammar.why: 'Eat' is irregular. In the past it is 'ate'.

grammar.q: Mum's soup is ___ than the soup in the cafe.
grammar.why: Long words use 'more' to compare: more delicious than.

grammar.q: I ___ have cereal for breakfast. I eat it every day!
grammar.why: 'Always' means every time. I eat it every day, so I always have it.

grammar.q: How often ___ you wash the dishes?
grammar.why: Ask with 'do' for I, you, we and they: How often do you...?

grammar.q: Last night I ___ a glass of milk before bed.
grammar.why: 'Drink' is irregular. In the past it is 'drank'.

reading.title: Pancakes for breakfast
reading.text: It's Saturday morning, and Tom and his dad are in the kitchen. They are going to make pancakes! Tom puts some flour, two eggs and some milk in a big bowl. Dad mixes them with a spoon, and then he cooks the pancakes. Tom eats his pancake with honey, but Dad has his with cheese. 'Mmm, delicious!' says Tom. After breakfast, they wash all the plates and bowls.

qs.q: What are Tom and his dad going to make?
How many eggs does Tom put in the bowl?
Tom mixes the eggs and the milk.
What does Tom eat his pancake with?
They wash the plates and bowls after breakfast.

reading.title: Grandma's vegetable soup
reading.text: Last Sunday, Mia visited her grandma. It was cold and rainy, so Grandma made her famous vegetable soup. Mia helped her. She washed the carrots and potatoes, and Grandma cut them. They put them in a big pot with some water and salt. The soup cooked for an hour. When it was ready, it was very hot, so they waited for ten minutes. Then they ate it with bread and cheese. It was the best soup in the world!

qs.q: What was the weather like last Sunday?
Mia cut the carrots and potatoes.
The soup cooked for an hour.
They waited ten minutes before they ate the soup.
What did they eat with the soup?

extra.q: I ___ a mistake and put salt in the cake!
extra.why: We say 'make a mistake', not 'do a mistake'.

extra.q: Please ___ the oven when you finish.
extra.why: 'Turn off' means stop a machine working.

extra.q: Put the milk back ___ the fridge, please.
extra.why: 'In' means inside: the milk goes in the fridge.

extra.q: I'm hungry, ___ I'm going to make a sandwich.
extra.why: Use 'so' to say what happens because of something: I'm hungry, so I'm making a sandwich.
